transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Title: Redwood migration demo: OpenAI+Anthropic+Together parity mapping
Attendees: Javier Morales (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE) — Sarah Kim (Nimbus Labs, Head of ML), Tom Delgado (Platform Eng), Maya Singh (Lead DS), Liam Park (Security)

Summary:
Quick migration-focused demo covering API parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood, console walkthrough (routing, rollouts), and Optimize recommendations (batching/quant, KV cache). Discussed hosting options (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and security controls (KMS, SOC2, audit logs). Agreed next steps: share parity spreadsheet, provision trial keys, run benchmarks, then POC scoping call.

-- Transcript (imperfect auto-transcript style, timestamps approximate) --
[00:00] Javier: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Javier from Redwood. We teamed up with Priya and Ethan; we're going to run through migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together into Redwood and show the API + Console + Optimize.
[00:12] Sarah: Thanks, Javier. We've been kicked off by Tom and Maya, we've been evaluating cost and latency mainly, also security — Liam is here to listen on that.
[00:18] Tom: Ya, hi. Our main ask is we need 95th percentile latency below 200ms for chat endpoints and <20ms embedding p50 basically, and cost needs to be less than our current run rate on OpenAI.
[00:29] Priya: Great — we'll try to show where Redwood maps features, and where there are trade-offs, e.g., quantization and dedicated pools. Quick note, some of the transcribed names may come out weird in the auto-thing, sorry if there are typos.

[03:05] Ethan: Ok jumping into the Console — two things to watch: model catalog mapping (we expose model aliases that map to open weights or tuned variants) and routing policies. So if you're migrating from say GPT-4 style calls, you can map to a Redwood-verified equivalent — we have a parity sheet we use.
[03:28] Maya: When you say parity, do you mean 1:1 token semantics, or response quality? Because our prompts rely on a lot of subtle system messages.
[03:35] Priya: Good q. Parity is twofold: 1) API semantics — request/response shape, function calling, streaming — we keep the same patterns; 2) model behavior — we provide recommended model choices and prompt tweaks. Usually we run a small eval set to check quality regressions.
[05:10] Sarah: What about Anthropic-specific safety layers — do you try to replicate that at the platform level?
[05:18] Javier: We don't rebrand someone else's safety model, but we support server-side filters, prompt templates, and can route to a model variant that has safety-oriented finetunes. Also, Optimize can detect regression against your evals and alert.

[08:02] Priya: API example — here's a live call: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"redwood-4o","messages":...}' — you'll see streaming tokens and chunking.
[08:28] Tom: Is the chat path identical to what we'd do with OpenAI's chat/completions?
[08:34] Priya: Pretty close. We support role-based messages, function calling, streaming — minor param name differences but we have a shim in our SDK to accept OpenAI-style params. So migration is often small code changes.

[12:45] Ethan: On embeddings we expose both dense and hybrid options; you can pin a specific embedding model and we support batch embedding with automatic retry logic. Latency will depend on whether you run hosted or dedicated.
[13:02] Maya: We use Together for some LLM workflows; they have a different tokenization that causes slight discrepancy in similarity scores — how do you handle that?
[13:12] Priya: We recommend running a small conversion and scoring job. For search embeddings we supply mapping guidance in the parity sheet and a small sample script to reindex.

[17:00] Javier: Security — Liam, I know you had questions earlier. We support SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. For Private deployment we can run in your VPC and integrate with your HSM.
[17:22] Liam: For KMS, are keys customer-controlled? And do logs include token-level metadata or full request payloads?
[17:32] Ethan: Keys can be customer-managed via KMS; logs can be configured to redacted or include headers only per your retention policy. We send SOC2 docs and an integration guide.

[22:10] Priya: Quick demo of Optimize: it surfaces batching recommendations based on your token distribution, suggests quantization profiles for candidate models, and shows caching opportunities — e.g., prefix/KV caching for chat sessions can reduce cost by 20–40% if you have many short-turn chats.
[22:40] Tom: That KV cache — is it safe to use with PII?
[22:46] Priya: It's configurable. For hosted we have tenant isolation and encryption at rest; for Private/Dedicated you can choose not to cache or to use in-memory cache only. We'll put specifics in the security doc.

[27:55] Maya: About model rollouts — can we do canary and automatic rollback on quality regressions?
[28:02] Javier: Yes, Console supports canary routes, percentage rollouts, and you can supply evaluation prompt sets for automatic quality checks. If a rollout causes a regression we can auto-fallback to prior variant.

[32:10] Priya: Demoing parity mapping sheet now — we show OpenAI endpoint -> Redwood mapping, Anthropic -> Redwood mapping, Together -> Redwood mapping. For example: OpenAI gpt-4o -> redwood-4o, Anthropic claude-internal -> redwood-c, Together x-xx -> redwood-t-1. The sheet includes recommended prompt adjustments and temperature mapping. (note: sample link in chat: https://redwood.ai/parity/nimbus-sample)
[32:45] Sarah: That sheet — will it include expected cost per 1k tokens comparisons?
[32:51] Javier: Yes, we can include a cost delta column based on your traffic profile. Priya will run two sample scenarios to show cost/latency trade-offs.

[36:30] Tom: About SLA: we probably need a contractual SLA for Dedicated. What are typical numbers?
[36:36] Javier: Dedicated SLA targets are 99.9% uptime with latency SLOs we can size for your throughput; we can include detailed SLOs in a proposal.

[39:58] Ethan: Quick note about infra — kernel selection and CUDA optimizations matter; when you migrate you may see differences in absolute latency depending on sequence length distribution. We usually pick kernels per workload.
[40:20] Maya: Will you help with model quantization? Our quantized models on-prem performed ok but with some accuracy loss.
[40:28] Priya: We run recommend profiles — e.g., 8-bit quant for embeddings, mixed 8/16 for chat — and include a quality regression report. Optimize will suggest quant profiles and show estimated cost savings.

[45:12] Liam: A couple security specifics — do you retain request payloads by default? How long and can we configure retention?
[45:22] Javier: Retention is configurable per-account; default is 30 days for hosted debug logs, longer for audit logs depending on plan. For Private you control retention entirely. We can also provide options to disable content retention.

[48:00] Sarah: Great — let's recap next steps before we run out of time.
[48:06] Javier: Recap: 1) I'll send the parity mapping spreadsheet and a sample prompt mapping doc; 2) Priya will provision trial API keys and run two sample benchmarks (chat and embeddings) and share results; 3) Tom will provide your production traffic profile and prompts; 4) Liam will send a short KMS/audit questions doc; 5) we'll schedule a POC scoping session the week of 7/29.
[48:42] Maya: Sounds good, thanks. Also please include the link to the Console demo recording and the Optimize example export.
[48:50] Javier: Will do. We'll also attach SOC2 and KMS integration notes.
[49:00] Tom: Timeline — if the trial looks good we'd like to start a pilot in August and then evaluate Dedicated by September.
[49:10] Javier: Understood. We'll follow up with those artifacts by Friday.

[51:30] Sarah: Thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[51:35] Priya: Thanks — talk soon.

-- End transcript --
